title: Gnotobiotic Growth Assay for Arabidopsis Root Microbiota Under Iron Limitation
author: Harbort, Hashimoto, et al.

steps.title: Prepare iron media
steps.instruction: Make two sterile agar‑based media each containing 100 µM iron and buffered to pH 7.4 with 10 mM HEPES; for the unavailable‑iron condition add FeCl₃ (iron III) as the iron source, and for the available‑iron condition add FeEDTA (ferric sodium ethylenediaminetetraacetate) as the chelated iron source.

steps.title: Surface‑sterilize and pre‑germinate seeds
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize Arabidopsis thaliana Col‑0 seeds, sow them on axenic growth medium containing vitamins and sucrose, and incubate for 5–6 days to obtain synchronized seedlings.

steps.title: Prepare SynCom inoculum
steps.instruction: Grow the rhizobacterial strains that compose the synthetic community (SynCom) originally isolated from Arabidopsis roots, combine them in the desired composition (full community, reduced set, or single strain) and keep the inoculum ready for plate inoculation.

steps.title: Inoculate media and transfer seedlings
steps.instruction: Add the SynCom inoculum to each iron‑condition plate, then transfer the pre‑germinated seedlings onto the plates, placing 5–6 individual plants per plate. Prepare three replicate plates per condition (total 15–18 plants per experiment).

steps.title: Grow plants and harvest tissues
steps.instruction: Incubate the plates under appropriate growth conditions until shoots develop, then harvest shoots for fresh‑weight measurement and collect leaf tissue for chlorophyll extraction, normalizing chlorophyll to the input sample weight.

steps.title: Analyze data statistically
steps.instruction: Plot shoot fresh weight with boxplots showing individual plant data points; plot chlorophyll content normalized to input weight as fresh‑weight‑based values. For shoot weight use non‑parametric tests (Kruskal‑Wallis, Wilcoxon signed‑rank, and/or Dunn’s pairwise comparison). For chlorophyll use ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD.

description: In this protocol, we will assess Arabidopsis thaliana accession Col-0 performance when grown axenically or in the presence of a synthetic community (SynCom) of bacteria on two media with contrasting iron availability: a replete, “available iron” condition and an iron-limiting “unavailable iron” condition. In this system, the concentration of iron is identical in both media (100 μM); the availability is varied by providing forms of iron that differ in their solubility at high pH. By buffering the media strongly at pH 7.4 with 10 mM HEPES, we mimic iron-limiting calcareous soils, where iron is present but unavailable to plants (Kobayashi and Nishizawa, 2012). In the “unavailable iron” condition, iron(III) (supplied as FeCl3) is sparingly soluble and is unavailable to plants. This is critical for assessing nutritionally beneficial host-microbiota interactions, which are precluded in artificial systems where iron is removed altogether (Harbort et al., 2020). As a control “available iron” medium with the same iron content and pH, the media is supplied with the same concentration of a chelated form of iron (FeEDTA, Ferric sodium ethylenediaminetetraacetate), which has increased solubility even in these alkaline conditions. To assess the impact of bacterial commensals on host performance in these conditions, the media are inoculated with a SynCom of rhizobacterial strains originally isolated from Arabidopsis roots grown in soil (Bai et al., 2015). Rhizobacterial culture collections of different origins can also be employed and compared. The complexity and diversity of the SynCom can be adjusted to suit the experimental question, or reduced to single strains in mono-associations. In this protocol, surface-sterilized seedlings are pre-germinated for 5–6 days on axenic growth medium containing vitamins and sucrose, and then transferred to experimental conditions with controlled iron availability and commensals.
